summary: Redesign the M13 RLM Settings > Plugins card into a simple-first, bilingual, DSH-token-aligned configuration surface. The Candidate separates common settings from limits/recovery/token guard, allows preconfiguration while globally disabled, makes only true feature dependencies conditional, adds human-readable unit hints, enables reset of existing user overrides, and replaces sequential field writes with one revision-fenced SettingsScope.mutate followed by raw-user-layer read-back verification so rejected/conflicting saves keep the draft.

pointers: every user-facing field has detailed bilingual help
Save is one revision-fenced atomic mutate with read-back verification
existing overrides can be reset before the user makes another edit
global enabled state does not disable every independent field

steps: Reviewed the current dsh-rlm M13 card/model/locales and the accepted #54 settings contract, then separated the UX work under Issue #75 from the runtime/protocol findings opened as successor Issues.

Reviewed current official DeepSeek Harness settings-card guidance and PluginCard styling: plugin cards own their chrome but should follow the --dsw-alias-* theme system; reviewed SettingsScope.mutate semantics and confirmed a Host rejection can recover/read-back while the Promise resolves.

Reworked the card into General, Limits, Recovery & safety, and Token guard sections with detailed EN/ZH guidance and readable seconds/KiB/MiB summaries. Independent settings remain editable while dsh-rlm is disabled; only durableRoot and maxQueryTokensPerCell follow their actual parent feature dependencies.

Changed Save to one SettingsScope.mutate operation fenced by the snapshot revision, then verify the accepted raw user layer before clearing dirty state. Existing overrides can be staged for reset even from an initially clean draft; Discard affects only local edits.

Added a focused source/locale regression file and included it in the repository full test script. The Candidate is intentionally limited to the settings client surface; runtime correctness fixes #68-#84 are not folded into this UI change.
